page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-64 is an Arm-based cloud server instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs built on 64-bit Arm architecture. The configuration pairs high-density multi-core compute capability with 512 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include integrated hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs.

Storage and networking architectures depend on external network-attached services, as the instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Users deploying stateful or disk-intensive applications must attach external persistent block storage to meet persistent data requirements.

From an infrastructure and efficiency standpoint, the 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides significant resource density for memory-bound applications without requiring x86 licensing overhead. The dedicated 64-core Arm allocation is suitable for large in-memory caching systems, distributed data processing engines, relational databases with extensive buffer pools, and large-scale compilation jobs that benefit from high parallel throughput alongside substantial memory capacity.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-64 is an Arm-based instance configured with 64 dedicated 64-bit Arm vCPUs and 512 GB of system memory. Designed with an expanded 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, it supplies 8 GB of RAM per dedicated vCPU, catering directly to memory-intensive software footprints. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units and features no onboard local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of external cloud storage volumes for file systems and databases. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned with the hardware profile. The high-capacity memory footprint combined with a substantial 64-core Arm processing pool establishes strong operational efficiency for enterprise in-memory caches, distributed memory computing, large transactional databases, and substantial analytical batch processes requiring extensive RAM buffers.
